messages:
noah: quick ping  spotted a leak in the Go generator when the constructor ctx cancels mid-handshake in our step-function sample. short repro below.
priya: can you drop the smallest repro + sdk version?
noah: vendored v0.14.1. minimal:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 25*time.Millisecond)
g, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, model, opts...)
// we call g.Stream() immediately
```
if ctx cancels during the websocket/http handshake, constructor may return but a read goroutine remains and GC doesn't collect it in CI.
aj: thanks. sounds like the reader is started before the handshake completion and lacks a cancel handle. two options: 1) delay spawning reader until handshake finishes, or 2) spawn it but tie it to a cancelable ctx owned by constructor.
priya: i tried option 2 locally: create childCtx, childCancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()) and pass childCtx into readLoop; call childCancel() when constructor errors. that stops the goroutine reliably.
noah: option 1 worked for me too (only start readLoop after handshake success). both are non-breaking.
aj: prefer option 2 in codebase since it centralizes cancellation logic and avoids flipping start-order assumptions. option 1 is simpler though. either way we need a deterministic unit test simulating slow handshake + cancel.
priya: added a small test harness that fakes a slow server and cancels constructor ctx; assert no goroutines leaked post-return. will add that to PR.
noah: also discovered some onboarding examples create generators with context.WithTimeout which is an anti-pattern for long-lived streams. we should update docs and add a linter/snippet check in examples.
aj: +1 on docs and linter. we should also document recommended patterns: either use background ctx for generator lifetime or explicitly Start/Stop if we add that API.
priya: regarding API surface: would it be worth adding a Start(ctx) so constructor is cheap? breaking change though. maybe add Start as opt-in, leave NewGenerator behavior unchanged.
aj: add Start as experimental in v0.15 RFC if we go that route. for current release do the cancellation-fix and test. then follow-up RFC for Start/Stop.
noah: opened PR "go: bind generator readLoop to constructor cancel + test" (#6321) with child-ctx approach + unit/integration tests + docs blurb. cc @aj @priya.
kelly-bot: CI for PR #6321 queued  running unit tests and the new slow-handshake test (flaky runner allowed 1 retry) :robot_face:
priya: after merge we should sweep internal sample repos and the quickstarts to replace short-lived timeouts. i'll add a chore ticket for that.
aj: also add a small note in CHANGELOG and migration guide about the fix and recommended ctx patterns.
noah: thanks — will follow up with the chore and link the PR once CI passes. :thumbsup:
